findings.title: The backward behaviour is wider than disclosed: on a record without first-recorded clocks the R7C-FREEZE-3 reading also fails full-dose and adverse answers when a week of the window was closed by a decision that records no gates
findings.summary: legacyUnreadWeeks takes the recorded gates of the decision that closed the week; a nonclinical exercise substitution at the end of a week closes it (WEEK_EVIDENCE, SUBSTITUTE_FOR_REASON) with gates null, so the legacy rule never reads that week as unread. On FREEZE-4 with every first-recorded clock removed (as the backward-behaviour test does), 128 of 224 cells keep the stale projection VALID: SHORT60 28, SHORT80 28, SHORT_ADVERSE 28, ADVERSE 20, LONGSHORT_REST_MISS 12, EXEC 8, MIX_SHORT_MISS 4 (by closer SUB 84, SCH 44), the same set as FREEZE-3. Example: GEN week 7, g=0, week 3 closed by a substitution, every gap run adverse, clinical substitution day 2, cleared, plain day 3: KEEP VALID QUALITY 34 / LONG 60, direct EASY 25 / LONG 35; R10K taper: QUALITY 25 / LONG 40 then a race touch, direct EASY 15 to the race. With clocks every such cell converges (0/224). The freeze record (phase7.metadata.backwardBehaviour), the handoff ('Backward behaviour', R5) and the source comment state the legacy reading is sound for full-dose and adverse answers and that only shortened late answers keep FREEZE-3's reading. Impact limited to records written before R7C-FREEZE-4 or rows a client injects into actualLedger without passing them as observations; the runtime is a shadow reference. Historical: the same cells show QE-R7C-07 was not closed at full dose on FREEZE-3 for windows with a gate-less closing decision (not tested by the Phase 6 review).

findings.title: Phase 7 extends the reach (QE-R7C-11) and the QE-R7C-12 re-plan to habitual late reporters whose runs are shortened: mid-week VALID raises of later conditional weeks above FREEZE-3 and above the week's own review, not disclosed
findings.summary: Habitual late reporter (strength on its day, weekly review day 6, runs reported day 1 of the next week), runs at 60 % or 80 %: FREEZE-3 reads the late shortened runs as read (HOLD either way), FREEZE-4 as unread (first recorded after the week's review), as the invariant requires. At full dose FREEZE-4 equals FREEZE-3. Shortened: the weekly run doses before each review are identical to FREEZE-3 and never above the timely path, but at the day-4 strength report FREEZE-4 makes 19 recorded re-plans where FREEZE-3 keeps (GEN and R10K, 4 paths), all VALID, re-planning later weeks' conditional projections: mostly downward (QUALITY -> EASY; R10K taper EASY 30 -> 15) with 16 same-role raises (EASY 41 -> 45 GEN 60 % weeks 6-9, EASY 46 -> 50, EASY 30 -> 35 week 11, LONG 62 -> 65 and 67 -> 70, LONG 40 -> 45 R10K 80 %), 14 of them above what the week's own review then plans for the same session, VALID from day 4 until that review. Mechanism: QE-R7C-12's (C9 leaves the week's elapsed unreported runs uncredited; the dose then comes from the single-run ceiling), now reached through QE-R7C-11's reach. The phase's differential late-reporter timeline makes only the day-1 delivery and the day-6 review per week, so it reports lateReporterShort identical; the handoff's '128/128 identical, the habitual late reporters (full dose and shortened) included' holds for that timeline only. Same class as QE-R7C-12; executed weeks never above the timely facts; not blocking.
